name: comp-264

frames.best_why: All three axis rows are visible with X dragged to 3 and ringed, so the slider-plus-field pairing is obvious.

tagline: Three stacked rows nudge an object on the X, Y and Z axes.
summary: A position panel with one slider and one small number box per axis. X, Y and Z can be dragged or typed, and a Reset button puts all three back to zero.
appearance: The heading Object position sits over three rows, each starting with a small grey letter, then a grey track with a white fill and round knob, then a narrow rounded box holding a number. A full-width outlined Reset button with a circular arrow closes the group.
behaviour: Dragging a knob shifts that axis and rewrites its box, while typing a number and confirming jumps the knob to match. Reset snaps X, Y and Z back to zero together.
demo_content: Axes labelled X, Y and Z opening at -2, 4 and 2, then both moved and reset to 0.
search_phrases: three sliders for x y and z
move an object along three axes
set coordinates in a design tool
rows of sliders with a reset button
align an element with numeric sliders
use_when: An editor needs to nudge an object on three axes and also type exact coordinates.
avoid_when: A single free 2D drag area is wanted; here each axis is its own separate row.
customise: Axis names, the minus ten to ten range, starting values and the reset target are written in the source; adding an axis means another block.
weight_why: Three small sliders, three inputs and a button; idle until touched.

a11y.note: The sliders are named X, Y and Z, but every number box is called Enter value, so they cannot be told apart.

issues: All three number fields share the same accessible name, so screen readers cannot distinguish the axes.
The heading uses a legend outside any fieldset.
polish_why: Even rows, consistent controls and a clear reset; small text stays legible.
